column3: Concatenate the original list with itself, preserving its order in both copies.
Scan the numbers with a set of earlier values. Report a duplicate before inserting the current value; otherwise finish with false.
Count each character in both strings and compare the complete frequency maps.
Scan left to right with a value-to-index map. Look up the current complement before storing the current index.
Compare each character position of the first string against every other string. Stop at the first mismatch or shorter string.
Sort each word's characters into a key, group original words by that key, then return the groups.
Scan every value while a separate write position advances only for values that should remain. Return the retained prefix length.
Keep a candidate and a balance: equal values reinforce it and different values cancel it. Replace the candidate when the balance reaches zero.
Hash each key into a bucket, then check the actual keys in that bucket. Add, remove, and query without confusing collisions with equality.
Hash keys into buckets of key-value pairs. Update a matching pair, append a new key, and search or remove by the full key.
Build an in-place max-heap. Move its root to the end of the unsorted prefix, shrink that prefix, and restore the heap.
Maintain regions for zeros, ones, and twos with three positions. Examine a swapped-in unknown value before advancing past it.
Count occurrences, place each distinct value into its frequency bucket, and collect values from the largest frequencies until k are chosen.
Encode each string as its length, a separator, and its contents. Decode by reading the length and then exactly that many characters.
Build a padded two-dimensional prefix-sum table. Answer each rectangle using four corners and inclusion-exclusion.
Store the product strictly before each index in a forward pass. Multiply by the product strictly after it in a backward pass.
Track seen digits separately for each row, column, and box. Ignore empty cells and reject a digit repeated in any of its three regions.
Put values in a set. Extend a consecutive run only from values whose predecessor is absent, and keep the longest run.
Add each positive difference between neighboring prices. This captures profitable rises while allowing multiple transactions.
Cancel values against two candidate balances. Recount the surviving candidates and keep only those occurring more than n/3 times.
Count earlier prefix sums, starting with one empty prefix. For each new prefix, add the count of prefix minus k before recording it.
Swap each value from 1 through n into index value minus one, stopping on duplicates. Find the first position whose expected value is missing.
Swap the first and last characters, then move both positions inward until they meet.
Move inward from both ends, skipping non-alphanumeric characters. Compare the remaining characters without case differences.
Compare opposite ends until the first mismatch. Test both remaining intervals obtained by deleting one of the mismatching characters.
Advance a shared character index and append from each string when that index exists. Continue until both strings are exhausted.
Compare the last unused values of both sorted inputs. Write the larger value into the last free slot of nums1 and work backward.
Scan the sorted array while tracking its unique prefix. Copy a value into the next output position only when it differs from the last retained value.
Compare the sum at the two ends of the sorted array with the target. Increase the smaller end or decrease the larger end, and return one-based positions.
Sort, fix one value, and search the remaining suffix with two inward-moving positions. Skip duplicate choices and duplicate matching pairs.
Sort, fix two distinct positions, and search the remaining suffix with two positions. Skip duplicate choices at each level.
Reduce k modulo the array length. Reverse the whole array, then reverse the first k values and the remaining values separately.
Measure the container between the outer lines. Keep the best area and move the shorter boundary inward.
Sort weights and always assign the heaviest remaining person a boat. Pair that person with the lightest only when their combined weight fits.
Track the highest boundary seen from each end. Process the side with the smaller boundary and accumulate the water above its next bar.
Keep a set of the previous at most k values. Check for the current duplicate, then insert it and remove the value that expires from the window.
Track the minimum price encountered so far. At each day, compare today's sale profit against the best earlier profit.
Expand a window of unique characters. Remove characters from its left until the next right character can be included without repetition.
Track character counts and the best frequency seen as the right boundary advances. Move the left boundary when length minus that frequency exceeds k.
Count the required characters and a fixed-length window in s2. Update entering and leaving counts and detect when all 26 counts match.
Expand the sum window to reach the target. Repeatedly shrink a valid window while recording its shortest length.
Search the possible starting positions of a k-element window. Compare the two competing boundary distances and keep the left window on ties.
Expand until all required character counts are covered. Shrink while coverage remains valid, keeping the shortest interval found.
Keep candidate indices in decreasing value order. Expire indices outside the window and discard smaller trailing candidates before reading the front maximum.
Keep the valid scores in a stack. Apply cancellation, doubling, or addition to the latest valid scores and sum the final stack.
Push opening brackets. Each closing bracket must match the latest opener, and no openers may remain at the end.
Push into an empty helper queue, then transfer the old active queue behind the new value. Swap queues so pop and top use the active front.
Push into an input stack. When the output stack is empty, transfer all inputs to reverse their order; pop and peek from the output stack.
Maintain value and running-minimum stacks at matching depths. Push and pop both so the latest minimum belongs to the current contents.
Push numbers; for each operator, pop right then left operand and push the computed result. Division truncates toward zero.
Keep surviving asteroids. Resolve collisions only when a new left-moving asteroid meets a right-moving survivor, continuing until one side survives.
Keep indices awaiting a warmer day in decreasing temperature order. A warmer day resolves trailing indices by their index distance.
Store price-span pairs in decreasing price order. Pop all prices no greater than the new price, add their spans, and store the combined span.
Process cars from nearest to farthest from the target. Add a new fleet only when its arrival time exceeds the fleet ahead.
Process slash-separated path components. Ignore empty and dot entries, pop for a parent step, and retain ordinary directory names.
Save the repetition count and previous text at each opening bracket. On a closing bracket, restore the outer text and append the repeated inner text.
Track each value's frequency and a stack for each frequency level. Pop from the highest frequency, using stack order to break ties by recency.
Keep indices of increasing bar heights. When a shorter bar arrives, resolve popped bars using their nearest shorter boundaries; a final zero flushes the stack.
Maintain an inclusive candidate interval. Compare its middle value, discard the impossible half including the checked middle, and return minus one if empty.
Find the first index whose value is at least the target. Use an upper boundary of n so insertion after the final value remains possible.
Search the integer range 1 through n. Use the guess API result to keep only the side that can contain the hidden number.
Find the first nonnegative integer whose square exceeds x. Return the preceding integer as the floor square root.
Search the matrix as one flattened sorted range. Convert each middle index to its row and column before comparing its value.
Search eating speeds from 1 to the largest pile. Sum each pile's rounded-up time and retain the smallest speed that finishes within h hours.
Search capacities from the largest package to the total weight. Greedily count ordered shipping days for each candidate capacity.
Compare the middle value with the rightmost value. Keep the side containing the rotation minimum, retaining the middle when it could be the answer.
Identify which half is sorted, then decide whether the target lies in that half's bounds. Search only the half that can contain it.
Search as a rotated array, but first skip an equal left boundary when duplicates hide the sorted half. Continue until a match or an empty range.
Append timestamped values per key. For a query, search that key's ordered history for the latest timestamp not exceeding the requested time.
Search the allowed maximum subarray sum. Greedily count contiguous groups for each bound and keep the smallest bound needing at most k groups.
Search a partition of the shorter array and derive the other partition's size. Once both left sides are no greater than both right sides, read the median boundaries.
Find the peak first. Search the increasing side before the decreasing side, reversing comparisons on the latter to preserve the smallest matching index.
Save the next node before reversing the current link. Advance previous and current pointers, then return the new head.
Append the smaller current node to a dummy-headed result. Advance only its input list and attach the unexhausted remainder at the end.
Advance one pointer by one link and another by two. A meeting proves a cycle; reaching a missing fast link proves termination.
Locate and detach the second half, reverse it, then alternate nodes from the first half and the reversed half.
Start two pointers at a dummy node with a gap of n plus one links. Move them together, then bypass the node after the slower pointer.
Create a clone for every original node in one pass. In a second pass, use the identity map to connect each clone's next and random links.
Traverse both digit lists together with a carry. Append a new digit for each sum and continue while either list or the carry remains.
Treat array values as next-node links. Find a cycle meeting, reset one pointer to the start, and move both one step to locate the duplicate entry.
Locate the node just before the reversal segment. Repeatedly detach the node after the segment's first node and insert it at the segment's front.
Keep a fixed array, head index, and item count. Compute rear positions modulo capacity and distinguish full from empty by the count.
Map keys to doubly linked nodes ordered by recency. Move accesses to the front and evict the tail's least recently used node when over capacity.
Track values, frequencies, and ordered keys within each frequency. Promote accesses and evict the oldest key at the lowest frequency.
Put each nonempty list's first node into a min-heap. Append the smallest node and add its successor until all lists are consumed.
Check that k nodes remain before reversing them. Connect the reversed group's old head to the recursively processed remainder; leave a short final group intact.
Use a stack to descend left, visit the popped node, then move right. This produces left-node-right order without recursion.
Visit each popped node, then push its right child before its left child. The stack therefore explores left before right.
Collect nodes in node-right-left order using a stack. Reverse the collected sequence to obtain left-right-node order.
At each node, swap its children and recursively invert both child subtrees. Return the original root reference.
Return zero for a missing node. Otherwise return one plus the larger depth of its two subtrees.
Return subtree heights upward. At each node, compare the sum of its two child heights with a separate global diameter.
Compute subtree heights after visiting their children. Propagate an unbalanced sentinel instead of a height if either child or their height difference is invalid.
Compare corresponding nodes, including missing children. Equal values are sufficient only when both corresponding subtrees also match.
Try a full structural comparison at each candidate root. If it fails, search both child subtrees for another starting point.
Move left when both targets are smaller and right when both are larger. The first split or target match is their lowest common ancestor.
Follow the value comparison down the tree. Create the new node at a missing child and reconnect the returned subtree on the way back.
Find the key by ordered comparisons. Replace a one-child node directly, or copy its inorder successor and delete that successor from the right subtree.
Process the queue in batches equal to its size at the start of each level. Record one value list per batch and enqueue its children.
Traverse one level at a time from left to right. Record only the final node of each level's queue batch.
Recursively build four equal quadrants. Collapse them into one leaf only when all four are leaves with the same value.
Carry the largest ancestor value separately down each root-to-node path. Count a node when its value is at least that maximum.
Carry strict lower and upper bounds inherited from all ancestors. Narrow the appropriate bound when validating each subtree.
Use iterative inorder traversal to visit BST values in ascending order. Count visits and return the kth node's value.
Read each root from preorder and locate it in an inorder index map. Recursively build the left inorder range before the right range.
For every node, compute two values: rob this node or skip it. Robbing requires skipped children; skipping permits each child's better option.
Process both children before deciding about their parent. Delete a target-valued node only after it has become a leaf.
Return the best single downward branch from each node. Separately update the best full path through the node using both nonnegative child contributions.
Serialize in preorder with explicit null markers. Deserialize by consuming the same token order recursively to rebuild both child positions.
Keep a min-heap containing the largest k stream values seen so far. Drop its smallest value on overflow and report its root.
Represent the largest stones with a max-priority heap. Remove the two heaviest and reinsert their positive difference until at most one remains.
Keep at most k points in a heap whose root is the farthest retained point. Remove that point on overflow and return the retained coordinates.
Convert kth largest to a zero-based sorted rank. Partition the current range into less-than, equal-to, and greater-than pivot regions, then keep the region containing that rank.
Count the most frequent tasks and how many share that frequency. Compare the cooldown block bound with the total task count to account for fully filled gaps.
Keep ordered tweets per user and followee sets. Merge the latest relevant tweets with a heap, advancing only the stream whose tweet was selected.
Sort tasks by arrival time and enqueue all currently available tasks. Run the smallest processing-time/index pair, or jump the clock forward when none is available.
Choose the most frequent available character while holding the previous character out of the heap for one turn. Reject an impossible dominant count first.
Prefer the most frequent remaining letter. If it would create three identical consecutive letters, use the next candidate or stop if none exists.
Record passenger changes at pickup and drop-off positions in a difference array. Accumulate occupancy in position order and reject any capacity excess.
Maintain a max-heap for the lower half and a min-heap for the upper half. Repair their ordering and balance their sizes before reading the middle value or values.
Sort projects by required capital. At each of at most k rounds, heap-select the largest profit among projects affordable with the current capital.
For each input value, recurse once excluding it and once including it in the running XOR. Sum the completed subset XOR values.
Record the current subset, then choose each later position in turn. Undo each appended value after exploring that branch.
Try sorted candidates from a nondecreasing start position. Recurse on the remaining target while allowing the same candidate to be reused.
Sort candidates, skip equal choices at the same depth, and advance past each chosen index. Record a combination when the remaining target reaches zero.
Choose increasing values from 1 through n until k are selected. Bound the next choice so enough values remain to complete the combination.
Build a full ordering by choosing any unused input index. Mark it during that branch, then undo both the choice and the mark.
Sort values and record each growing subset. Skip equal alternatives at the same recursion depth, while allowing distinct duplicate positions in deeper levels.
Sort values and track used positions. At a given depth, skip a duplicate whose equal predecessor has not been chosen, then undo usage on return.
Grow the string with an opener only while fewer than n are used. Add a closer only when unmatched openers remain.
Try each cell as a start and match one word character per adjacent move. Mark the current cell during a path and restore it when that path returns.
Try every palindromic prefix of the unprocessed suffix. Recurse from its end and undo the chosen piece before trying another cut.
For each digit, choose one mapped letter and advance to the next digit. Record the string only after all digits have contributed.
Check the total can form four equal sides, then place longest sticks first. Try each fitting side and undo failed placements, skipping equal side states.
Check divisibility and try larger values first. Place each value into a bucket without exceeding the target, undo failures, and skip equal bucket states.
Place one queen per row while tracking occupied columns and both diagonals. Undo each placement before exploring the next column and save complete boards.
Try one safe column for each row using column and diagonal sets. Undo each choice and sum one for every completed placement.
Memoize all valid sentences beginning at each string index. Join a dictionary prefix with each sentence returned for the remaining suffix.
Follow or create one character edge at a time. Mark complete words separately so a stored prefix is not automatically a complete word.
Store words in a trie with end markers. During search, follow a literal edge or explore all character children for a dot wildcard.
Let each prefix store its minimum number of extra characters. Either pay for its last character or attach a dictionary word to an earlier solved prefix.
Build a trie for all target words and search board paths through its prefixes. Mark cells per path, emit each terminal word once, and prune exhausted branches.
Add four sides for each land cell. Subtract two for each land neighbor already visited above or to its left.
Map each alien character to its rank. Compare adjacent words at their first different character, also rejecting a longer word before its exact prefix.
Subtract outgoing trust and add incoming trust for each person. Find a balance of n minus one, which requires all others' trust and no outgoing trust.
Scan for unvisited land; each such cell starts one island. Flood its connected land and mark it before exploring neighbors.
Flood each unvisited land component and sum its cells. Mark cells on entry and keep the largest component area.
Map original nodes to clones before exploring their neighbors. Reuse an existing clone when a cycle reaches a node already discovered.
Seed the queue with every gate at distance zero. Expand into unfilled rooms, assigning each its first and therefore shortest distance.
Start with every rotten orange and count the fresh ones. Spread rot one queue layer per minute, marking new rotten cells immediately.
Explore backward from each ocean border toward equal or higher cells. Return cells reached by both independent traversals.
Mark every region connected to a border O as safe. Flip the remaining O cells and restore the safe marks.
Explore lock states by increasing move count. Generate one-wheel neighbors, skip dead or visited states, and stop at the target.
Build prerequisite-to-course edges and indegrees. Repeatedly remove zero-indegree courses; all courses must be removed for the schedule to be feasible.
Queue every zero-indegree course and record the removal order. Release dependents as their indegrees reach zero; return no order if a cycle remains.
Traverse the undirected graph while remembering each node's parent. Reject a visited non-parent neighbor and require every node to be reached.
Run a reachability traversal from each course and record which courses it reaches. Answer each prerequisite query from that directed reachability table.
Start a traversal from every still-unvisited vertex, counting one component each time. Mark and explore its entire undirected component.
Try candidate edges from last to first. Search for a path between their endpoints while skipping the candidate edge; the first remaining path identifies the answer.
Connect email addresses belonging to the same account. Traverse email components, sort their addresses, and attach the associated account name.
Build reciprocal weighted edges for each equation. Traverse from each query source while multiplying edge ratios, returning minus one when no path exists.
Collect all leaves and remove them in simultaneous layers. Stop when the tree has only one or two central vertices remaining.
Group words by one-character wildcard patterns. Explore undiscovered neighboring words in distance layers and return the first layer containing the target.
Use a min-heap ordered by path effort. Relax a neighbor with the maximum of current effort and the new height difference, keeping the smallest effort per cell.
Use a min-heap to settle earliest arrival times from the start. Expand directed weighted edges and return the latest settled time only if every node is reached.
Order outgoing destinations lexically and consume each ticket during recursive traversal. Append airports when their outgoing tickets are exhausted, then reverse the route.
Sort all Manhattan-distance edges. Accept the next cheapest edge only when its endpoints are not yet connected, using BFS to check connectivity.
Expand the cell with the smallest required water level from a min-heap. A neighbor's path cost is the larger of the current level and its elevation.
Extract precedence from the first differing letters of adjacent words. Reject invalid prefixes, then remove zero-indegree letters to form an order or detect a cycle.
Relax every flight for exactly k plus one rounds. Read the previous round's prices and write a copy so one round adds at most one edge.
Compute the minimum spanning-tree cost, then recompute while excluding or forcing each edge. Compare costs to classify critical and optional minimum-tree edges.
Topologically order the row and column conditions independently. If neither has a cycle, place each number at the intersection of its two order positions.
Connect indices sharing a prime factor through one representative per factor. Traverse that graph and require every index to be reachable.
Track the counts for two neighboring stair states. Replace them with their sum and the previous value until the requested step count is reached.
Work backward, adding the cheaper of the next two finishing costs to each stair. Choose the cheaper of starting at stair zero or one.
Handle the three initial Tribonacci values. Repeatedly shift a three-value window and append the sum of its previous values.
Track the best totals for the previous two prefixes. At each house, choose between skipping it and adding it to the best total two houses back.
Handle a single house directly. Otherwise solve the linear robbery recurrence once without the first house and once without the last, taking the better result.
Expand matching characters around every single-character and adjacent-pair center. Keep the longest interval found.
Expand around every odd and even center. Count each successful expansion as one palindromic substring occurrence.
Work backward over suffixes, with one way to decode the empty suffix. Add valid one-digit and two-digit continuations, assigning zero to a leading zero.
Store the fewest coins needed for each amount, starting at zero coins for amount zero. Try every fitting coin as the final coin of that amount.
Track both largest and smallest products ending at the current position. A negative value can exchange their roles, while zero starts a new segment.
Mark the empty prefix as segmentable. A longer prefix is segmentable when it ends with a dictionary word after an already segmentable prefix.
Maintain the smallest possible tail for each increasing-subsequence length. Binary-search where each value replaces a tail or extends the list.
Reject an odd total. Track achievable sums while processing each value once and test whether half of the total can be reached.
Count ordered ways to reach each amount. For every increasing amount, try each number as the final element and add the ways for the remaining amount.
Store the fewest squares needed for each total. Try every square no larger than the current total as its final summand.
Handle the smallest mandatory splits, then take factors of three while the remainder exceeds four. Multiply by the final remainder instead of leaving a factor of one.
Work backward with the best score difference for the current player. Try taking one, two, or three stones and subtract the opponent's remaining advantage.
Store path counts for one row. Update each interior column by adding the count from its left to the count retained from above.
Maintain one row of path counts. Reset obstacle cells to zero; otherwise add the left count to the count already coming from above.
Accumulate minimum path sums in the grid from top-left to bottom-right. Each cell adds its cost to the better reachable predecessor above or left.
Compare string prefixes in a two-dimensional table. Matching last characters extend the diagonal; mismatches choose the better prefix after dropping one character.
Track achievable subset sums no greater than half the total stone weight. Use the largest such sum to minimize the difference between two groups.
Track holding, just-sold, and resting profits for each day. Compute new states only from previous-day states so buying cannot violate the cooldown.
Start with one way to form amount zero. Process each coin outside the increasing-amount loop so combinations are counted without ordering duplicates.
Map each reachable sum to its number of sign assignments. For each number, build a new map by adding both its positive and negative contributions.
Use states for consumed prefixes of both source strings. Extend a reachable state when the next character from either source matches the combined string.
Solve intervals from short to long using score advantage. Taking either end gains that pile and subtracts the opponent's best advantage on the remaining interval.
Memoize the best score by pile index and M, using suffix totals. Try each permitted take and subtract the opponent's best score from the remaining total.
Memoize the longest increasing path starting at each cell. Explore only strictly larger neighbors and reuse each cell's solved result.
Count ways to match each target prefix from each source prefix. Always allow skipping the source character and add a matching-use branch when characters agree.
Build edit distances between prefixes, including empty-prefix costs. Matching characters use the diagonal; others take one plus the best insert, delete, or replace state.
Solve intervals by choosing which balloon bursts last inside each interval. Combine its left and right subinterval results with the fixed outer boundaries.
Track which string and pattern prefixes match. A star either removes its preceding token or consumes another matching character while retaining that token.
Track available five- and ten-dollar bills in customer order. For twenty dollars, prefer ten plus five when possible, preserving more five-dollar bills.
Track a contiguous running sum and the best nonempty sum. Discard a negative running prefix before extending with the next value.
Compute maximum and minimum contiguous sums plus the total. Compare the normal maximum with total minus the minimum, handling all-negative input separately.
Track turbulent lengths ending in an upward or downward comparison. Extend the opposite direction on a strict change and reset both on equality.
Scan only as far as the reachable frontier permits. Extend that frontier with each reachable index's jump and reject an unreachable gap.
Track the farthest index reachable within the current jump layer. When the layer ends, count one jump and advance its boundary.
Track how many reachable earlier positions lie within the allowed jump-distance window. A new position is reachable only when that count is positive and its character is zero.
Reject insufficient total gas. Scan the surplus and restart just after a negative running segment, since none of that segment's starts can finish it.
Count cards and repeatedly start a group at the smallest remaining card. Consume exactly one of each required consecutive value or reject a missing card.
Queue each party's turn indices. The earlier queued senator bans the opponent and rejoins one full round later; continue until one party's queue is empty.
Discard any triplet that exceeds a target coordinate. Among the remaining triplets, require an exact match for each target coordinate somewhere.
Record each character's final position. Expand a partition's end to include every character encountered, closing it when the scan reaches that end.
Maintain the smallest and largest possible unmatched-open counts. Clamp the minimum to zero, reject a negative maximum, and require a possible zero at the end.
Assign one candy each, then satisfy increasing ratings from left to right. Sweep right to left, increasing only as needed to satisfy the other neighbor too.
Keep intervals before the new one unchanged, merge every overlap into the new interval, then append it before the untouched later intervals.
Sort by start time. Extend the last merged interval when the next one overlaps, otherwise start a new output interval.
Sort intervals by start. On overlap remove one and keep the smaller end; otherwise retain the new interval and update the tracked end.
Sort meetings by start time. Reject when a meeting starts before the previous meeting ends.
Process meetings by start time with a heap of room availability times. Reuse the earliest available room or allocate another, retaining one heap entry per room.
Keep available rooms ordered by number and busy rooms by finish time then number. Preserve meeting duration when delaying, and count assignments per room.
Sort intervals and queries. Add intervals whose start has been reached, discard expired heap candidates, and read the shortest remaining interval for each query.
Convert a one-based column number into base-26 letters. Subtract one before each remainder and reverse the collected least-significant letters.
First check that the two concatenation orders match. If they do, return a prefix whose length is the greatest common divisor of both lengths.
For each original adjacent node pair, insert a node holding their GCD. Advance to the saved original next node so inserted nodes are not processed again.
Create a new matrix with swapped dimensions. Read original row-column coordinates in reversed order for each output cell.
Transpose the square matrix across its main diagonal, swapping each pair once. Reverse every row to complete the clockwise rotation.
Traverse the current top, right, bottom, and left boundaries in order. Shrink each boundary and guard against re-reading a collapsed row or column.
Remember whether the first row and column originally contain zeros. Use their remaining cells as markers, clear marked interiors, then handle those first boundaries.
Apply the digit-square-sum transition once to a slow state and twice to a fast state. Stop at one or a repeated meeting state.
Propagate one carry from the final digit toward the front. Stop at the first digit below nine, or prepend one if every digit overflowed.
Read symbols from left to right. Subtract a symbol when the following symbol is larger; otherwise add it.
Handle a negative exponent by inverting the base. Repeatedly square the base, halve the exponent, and multiply the result for set exponent bits.
Multiply each digit pair into its aligned output positions. Split each accumulated value into a digit and a carry, then remove leading zeros.
Count stored point multiplicities and index horizontal partners. For each nonzero side, multiply the counts of the three required corners above and below the query.
XOR every number into an accumulator. Equal pairs cancel, leaving the value that appears once.
Repeatedly clear the lowest set bit with n AND n-minus-one. Count how many clear operations occur before n becomes zero.
Build bit counts from zero upward. Reuse the count for the number shifted right once, then add its lowest bit.
Add the two strings from right to left with a binary carry. Emit each result bit, continue through any final carry, then reverse the collected bits.
Repeat exactly 32 times: shift the result left, append the input's lowest bit, and shift the input right.
XOR the full index range with the array values. Values appearing on both sides cancel, leaving the missing number.
Compute sum-without-carry using XOR and carry using AND shifted left. Repeat under a 32-bit mask, then convert the result back to a signed integer.
Extract signed decimal digits using division toward zero. Check both 32-bit overflow boundaries before appending each digit to the reversed result.
Shift both endpoints right until their prefixes agree. Restore that common prefix's position with zeros in the varying lower bits.
Start with every bit of x present. Insert the bits of n minus one into x's zero-bit positions from low to high without changing x's set bits.
